what: blaze-stencil: the `tail` calling convention in the glue on x86-64 and AArch64, as Cranelift 0.137 lowers it (isa/{x64,aarch64}/abi.rs, machinst/abi.rs): its argument registers, callee-popped stack arguments (`ret imm16` on x86-64), every register clobbered across a call, the prologue growing the incoming argument area to tail_args_size, and `return_call`/`return_call_indirect` moving the arguments into that area, restoring the frame and jumping; calls between `tail` and native functions both ways. Until it lands, frame.rs (x86-64) and glue.rs (AArch64) stop naming the `tail` function and the instruction (no fallback). Tests: tests::func::calls::run::return_calls_cross_both_ways and return_calls_grow_and_shrink_stack_arguments, arch::x64::tests::refuses_what_cranelift_refuses (its `tail` case moves to a passing one). Needed by explicit_tail_calls / `become` (superset-of-rust).
